braceExpander.title: Brace Expander
braceExpander.description: Expand one template into a full list, using bash brace expansion
braceExpander.metaTitle: Brace Expander - Expand one template into a full list with ranges, steps and lists
braceExpander.metaDescription: Expand one template into a full list: write f{1..100}pd_ever_od30_{tag,bal} and get every combination, with bash brace expansion syntax. Ranges, steps, zero-padding, lists and multi-line templates, processed locally.

faq.q: How do I generate 100 field names at once?
faq.a: Write f{1..100}pd_ever_od30_tag. {1..100} is an integer range, {tag,bal} is a list, and multiple braces are combined automatically.

faq.q: Can ranges take a step or zero-padding?
faq.a: Yes. {1..100..2} steps by 2, and {001..100} pads to three digits (width comes from the starting value), so f{001..100} gives f001…f100.

faq.q: How do I get all tag rows before all bal rows?
faq.a: Switch Output order to Grouped in Advanced settings (the rightmost variable finishes completely before advancing); or write multiple template lines that expand independently.
Bash brace expansion: integer ranges, letter ranges {a..e}, steps, zero-padding and lists. \{ \} \, escape the braces and comma. Output matches bash line for line.

faq.q: How do I control the order of multiple variables?
faq.a: Use the **Output order** switch under the template. **Interleave** matches bash (f1_tag, f1_bal, f2_tag…); **Grouped** runs the rightmost variable all the way through, so every tag row comes first and every bal row after. Both modes produce the same items — only the order differs.

features: Expand from a single template using bash brace expansion
Integer and letter ranges, steps, zero-padding and lists
Multiple brace groups combine automatically; multi-line templates concatenate in order
Line separator plus whole-string prefix and suffix, ready for SQL IN or INSERT
Keep frequently used templates in history and reuse them in one click
Capped at 10,000 lines with a clear message instead of silent truncation
Switch between interleaved and grouped: f{1..4}_{tag,bal} gives eight alternating rows either way, or every tag row first and then every bal row.
